item.title: [DW] EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack using AI tools

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Ukraine’s former defence chief predicts new EU security alliance, gives behind-the-scenes look at Russia diplomacy
item.description: What happens behind the scenes at peace talks with Russia and in negotiations with allies? Oleksii Reznikov, Ukrainian defence minister at the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022, spoke candidly about his time leading his country's defence efforts. Now lecturing university students about negotiating tactics, he says Europe might soon see a new security alliance.

With 140 seats in the 250-seat assembly, the movement now faces the challenge of forming a government, tackling corruption and delivering domestic reforms. But its diverse political factions remain divided over Serbia’s future relationship with the EU and Russia.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘There is nothing soft about Russian soft power’: Ukraine institute director on the battle to re-name streets honouring Pushkin and other Russian figures
item.description: Should Russian cultural figures continue to be celebrated in European public spaces? Should streets named after Pushkin be renamed? Where do we draw the line between rejecting Russian imperialism and preserving Russian cultural heritage? These are some of the questions director general of the Ukrainian Institute Volodymyr Sheiko discusses with EUobserver.

item.title: [DW] North Macedonia remains stalled on its EU path after 21 years as a candidate

item.title: [DW] German police respond to multiple school bomb threats

item.title: [EU Observer] Kaliningrad is the Achilles’ heel of Putin in the Baltic Sea

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Could Czech public media lose their independence?
item.description: 205 crowns, or 8.20 euros, is what Czech households pay each month to fund their public broadcasting service. But this licence fee could soon be abolished. This decision is causing concern both within and outside the country. To the point that the European Commission has sent warnings about it.

item.title: [EU Observer] Hundreds of methane leaks uncovered in Europe, as Brussels delays monitoring crackdown
